# dependencytrack_workload_identity_binding (Resource)

Manages a Workload Identity Binding, which allows tokens from a Workload Identity Provider matching a subject to authenticate as a Service Account. Bindings cannot be modified, so any change replaces the binding. Requires API >= 5.2.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dependencytrack_service_account" "example" {
  name = "ci-pipeline"
}

resource "dependencytrack_workload_identity_provider" "example" {
  name     = "github-actions"
  type     = "OIDC"
  issuer   = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
  audience = "https://dependency-track.example.com"
}

# Allow any workflow in the acme-inc/app repository, when running on the main branch.
resource "dependencytrack_workload_identity_binding" "example" {
  service_account = dependencytrack_service_account.example.name
  provider_name   = dependencytrack_workload_identity_provider.example.name
  subject         = "repo:acme-inc/app:*"
  condition       = "claims.ref == \"refs/heads/main\""
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `provider_name` (String) Name of the Workload Identity Provider whose tokens are trusted.
- `service_account` (String) Name of the Service Account which the binding authenticates as, without the `svc:` prefix.
- `subject` (String) The `sub` claim to match, such as `repo:acme/app:ref:refs/heads/main`. A trailing `*` makes it a prefix match, whose prefix must end with `:` or `/`, such as `repo:acme/app:*`. For SPIFFE providers, the prefix must end with `/`.

### Optional

- `condition` (String) Optional CEL expression over the token's claims which must evaluate to true, with the claims available as the `claims` map, such as `claims.ref == "refs/heads/main"`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (Number) Timestamp of when the Workload Identity Binding was created, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
- `id` (String) Identifier for the Workload Identity Binding, in the format <ServiceAccountName>/<UUID>.
- `uuid` (String) UUID for the Workload Identity Binding as generated by DependencyTrack.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import using the Service Account name and the Binding UUID.
terraform import dependencytrack_workload_identity_binding.example ci-pipeline/01a0f908-4801-78c5-a1aa-8ebf50e1d193
```
